reasons: Exact bug and unaffected output lines matched the shared three-version Docker replay.

Root cause confirmed by source diff and by a targeted, self-checking dynamic PoC. The PoC forces the specific allocation performed inside lh_DECODER_CACHE_ENTRY_insert() to fail (via a malloc hook matched by exact call-site file:line, touching no other allocation), driving OSSL_DECODER_CTX_new_for_pkey() into the intro commit's newly-added error branch while cache->lock is held for write. A subsequent, ordinary call to the same API (no induced failure) serves as the oracle: it must succeed promptly if the lock was released. Running the identical sequence against all three built revisions (3 repetitions each, fully reproducible) gives a clean 3-way split: pre_intro never reaches the buggy branch at all (no error handling on insert failure existed) and the lock is always released, so the probe call always succeeds; post_intro takes the new error branch, leaks cache->lock, and the probe call fails every time (fast failure rather than a hang, matching the original reporter's account of an EBUSY-style same-thread re-lock failure); post_benign takes the same error branch but its added CRYPTO_THREAD_unlock() releases the lock, so the probe call succeeds every time, exactly matching the fix commit message ("never unlocked a write lock we were holding ... Fix it by ensuring the lock is released in the error path"). intro_verified=yes and benign_verified=yes with high confidence.

agent_oracle.description: Custom poc.c linked against libcrypto: installs a CRYPTO_set_mem_functions malloc hook that fails exactly one allocation, matched precisely by call-site file:line (crypto/lhash/lhash.c:114, the node allocation inside OPENSSL_LH_insert). It (1) warms up caches with OSSL_DECODER_CTX_new_for_pkey(keytype="RSA", selection=EVP_PKEY_KEYPAIR); (2) makes a "triggering" call with selection=EVP_PKEY_PUBLIC_KEY (a new cache key) with the failing allocator armed, forcing lh_DECODER_CACHE_ENTRY_insert() to fail while cache->lock is held for write; (3) makes a third "probe" call identical to the triggering call but with no induced failure (bounded by alarm(8)). On a correct build the probe call must promptly return a non-NULL OSSL_DECODER_CTX because cache->lock must have been released after the triggering call regardless of its outcome. Same binary/same 3-call sequence run unmodified against pre_intro, post_intro, and post_benign builds (ASan+UBSan), 3 repetitions each, fully deterministic.
agent_oracle.target_evidence: Source diff: post_intro (3d254b31344e) added in OSSL_DECODER_CTX_new_for_pkey() (crypto/encode_decode/decoder_pkey.c), after CRYPTO_THREAD_write_lock(cache->lock) and lh_DECODER_CACHE_ENTRY_insert(): `if (lh_DECODER_CACHE_ENTRY_error(cache->hashtable)) { ctx = NULL; ERR_raise(...); goto err; }`, and the shared `err:` label never calls CRYPTO_THREAD_unlock(cache->lock) (only decoder_cache_entry_free()/OSSL_DECODER_CTX_free()) -- a genuine lock leak, unlike every earlier goto-err site in the function which precedes the lock acquisition. post_benign (fix tree, same as parent 643f542a89be) inserts `CRYPTO_THREAD_unlock(cache->lock);` immediately before that ERR_raise/goto err. pre_intro (643f542a89be) lacks this check/branch entirely; insert failures are silently ignored and the lock is always released at the function's normal unlock. Dynamic evidence: identical 3-call PoC sequence, run 3x per version under ASan/UBSan. post_intro: triggering call returns NULL (error branch taken); probe call (no induced failure) also returns NULL every time, with libcrypto error queue pointing at decoder_pkey.c:847/765 -- consistent with the still-held write lock causing the re-lock attempt to fail, matching the reporter's own description of an EBUSY/assert on re-locking in the same thread. pre_intro: triggering call returns non-NULL (insert failure silently ignored, since the check doesn't exist yet); probe call succeeds every time. post_benign: triggering call returns NULL (same error handling as post_intro) but probe call succeeds every time (lock correctly released by the added unlock call).
